lines.text: Ben-hadad of Aram besieged Samaria with thirty-two kings and demanded Ahab's silver, gold, wives and children.
Ahab agreed to the first demand, but after the elders advised him, he refused the second demand to search his palace.
Ben-hadad swore Samaria would be reduced to dust, and he heard Ahab's reply while praying in his tent.
A prophet told Ahab the LORD would give him victory through the young officers, and Ahab gathered 232 officers and 5,000 troops.
The Israelites struck down their opponents and the Arameans fled, but Ben-hadad escaped on horseback with the cavalry.
